2. b) Prove that 3n + 5 ≠ Ω(n^2). -2.5 marks Big-Omega Notation Definition:
f(n)=Ω(g(n)) if there exist positive constants c and n0 such that f(n) ≥ c ⋅ g(n) for all n≥n0
This means there exist constants c > 0 and n0 such that: 3n + 5 ≥ c ⋅ n 2
Divide both sides by n 2 : 3n+5 / n2 >= c
As n approaches infinity, both 3/n and 5/n 2 approach 0.
Thus, 3/n+5/n 2 approaches 0, which contradicts the condition that it should be greater than or equal to some positive constant c.
Therefore, the assumption that 3n + 5 = Ω(n 2 ) is false, Hence, 3n+5 ≠ Ω(n 2 ).
